# T-2: Add regression classification

<!-- Auto-generated by `sdd-forge spec render` from spec.json.tasks[]. Do not edit manually. -->

## Goal
Classify changed files and discover the root regression command deterministically.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Config, package-json, composer-json, and makefile command discovery precedence is tested.
- package.json, composer.json, and Makefile discovery execute deterministic wrapper argv commands and do not shell-parse discovered script bodies.
- test.projectPaths targeted classification is tested for exact files, directory prefixes, renames, and deletes.
- active spec-local tests under specs/<active-spec>/tests/** do not trigger project regression unless matched by test.projectPaths.
- targeted mode is selected only when every trigger-relevant file is classified by test.projectPaths.
- target_paths are appended as separate argv tokens after the parsed root command; otherwise full mode is used.
- Unknown regular files force full regression.
- mixed docs/spec-artifact/non-project changes produce mixed-non-trigger when no project regression trigger exists.
- test-execute and gate-impl use the same status-aware changed-file helper.
- changed_files[] uses a stable sorted trigger-relevant snapshot with {status,path} or {status:"renamed",old_path,path}.

## Implementation Notes
Add helpers for command tokenization, path normalization, changed-file enumeration, generated artifact exclusion, and classifier decisions. Reuse or extend src/lib/git-helpers.js so status, rename, and untracked normalization is shared by execution and gate freshness checks. Parse only explicit test.command. For discovered ecosystem commands, execute npm test --, composer run-script test --, or make test argv wrappers and store script or target text as metadata. Apply test.projectPaths-proven test-file classification before generic analysis project-file triggers. Do not infer Python commands.

## Test Strategy
Unit tests for command grammar, discovery, changed-file status merging, and classifier categories.
